facts.statement: Dzungarisuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of crocodile.
facts.quote: Dzungarisuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of crocodile.

facts.statement: The only known remains of Dzungarisuchus consist of isolated postcranial bones and jaw fragments.
facts.quote: The only remains that have been found have been isolated postcranial and jaw fragments.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dzungarisuchus have been discovered in Xinjiang, China, dating to the late Eocene.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Xinjiang, China of late Eocene age.

facts.statement: The genus Dzungarisuchus was described by Dong in 1974.
Dzungarisuchus belongs to the subfamily Crocodylinae.
Dzungarisuchus is classified within the family Crocodylidae.
Dzungarisuchus lived during the Priabonian stage, between 37.71 and 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Priabonian to Priabonian (37.71 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: All fossil material discovered so far belongs to the type species Dzungarisuchus manacensis.
facts.quote: All material yet found has been referable to the type species, Dzungarisuchus manacensis.
